set.pl: Graue Mill, 3800 York Rd at Salt Creek, Fullersburg / Oak Brook (museum; forest preserve, look only)
pinev: Chicago Tribune 1934 places the mill on Salt Creek at York and Spring roads, the Graue Mill site; pin on Graue Mill, 3800 York Rd (41.8206, -87.9275, agrees with the Wikipedia longitude), r150.

set.pl: Corner of secs 2, 3, 10 and 11, T1N R7E, Lyon Twp, Oakland Co, on the Grand River plank road about 1 mi E of New Hudson; today the junction of South Hill Rd and Grand River Ave

pinev: Burrell 1909, Clay chapter: he 'sold his place in Clay' and on the gallows said he had buried $5,000 'at the foot of a red oak tree in the northwest corner of section 16 in Iowa'. No period paper yet.

Burrell's 1844 township list gives Iowa as T76-77N R6W; Highland (T77N R6W) was split off in 1854. Two readings: 'in Iowa' as the state puts the oak in Clay Twp, the chapter the story is told in; as Iowa Twp (T76N R6W after 1854, T77N R6W before) it lies 20 mi NE. Primary pin Clay: sec 16 T74N R9W from BLM PLSS (box 41.2061-41.2211 / -91.9071 to -91.8876), pin just inside the NW corner.
1906 Washington Co atlas, Clay Twp (Ancestry image 31617_072148-00043): the NW of sec 16 is cut into small Morgan family lots (C. B. Morgan and others), so the corner was built up by 1906.

Alternative reading: 1906 Washington Co atlas, Iowa Twp plate (Ancestry image 31617_072148-00030): the NW of sec 16 is D. Craig 80 with an Albert Schnoebelen strip, J. R. Webster estate 200 to the S with a pond, English River on the N edge, no timber symbol.
Sec 7 T1N R8E centre from BLM PLSS (box 42.5614-42.5763 / -89.6025 to -89.5832); the Census place centroid for Juda (42.5900, -89.5092) also falls in sec 2 of T1N R8E; r800.

1873 Green Co atlas, Jefferson Twp (Ancestry image 31617_072128-00299) confirms Jefferson = T1N R8E; sec 7 owners in 1873 were G. Eley, P. Connell, Frederick, Batton, J. Blummer and W. Carter, with no Lake, as expected 34 years on.
